To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) In the normal dorsal root ganglia, TGF-alpha is expressed mainly in small DRG neurons, and its receptor, EGF receptor, is expressed mainly in large or medium-sized DRG neurons and in satellite glial cells surrounding these neurons.

TGF-alpha is expressed in DRG neurons and satellite cells in the normal state and is up-regulated after peripheral nerve injury, suggesting that TGF-alpha plays a role in the survival and plasticity of DRG neurons and in the proliferation of satellite cells after peripheral nerve injury.
TGF-alpha and TGF-alpha receptor are expressed differentially in the DRG neurons and glia after peripheral nerve transection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of nerve repair.
the role of the TGF-α system in the dorsal root sensory neurons in response to sciatic lesion.
the mechanisms of neuronal and glial plasticity in the peripheral nervous system following injury, with a special focus on TGF-alpha and the EGF receptor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TGF-alpha and TGF-beta play a key role in the regeneration of the peripheral nerves.
TGF-α is involved in the satellite cell activation and proliferation and neuronal survival after peripheral nerve lesion.

the up-regulation of EGF receptor and TGF-alpha in the DRGs following sciatic nerve lesion is likely to be a result of the activation of satellite cells and neurons, and that this up-regulation may be important in the plastic changes of the DRG neurons following peripheral nerve injury.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the differential expression of TGF-alpha in the satellite cells and neurons of the DRG may be a key mechanism underlying the differential plasticity of neurons and glia in the DRG in response to nerve injury.
TGF-alpha is expressed mainly by satellite cells in the normal DRG, while EGF receptor is mainly expressed by neurons.
TGF-alpha is up-regulated in satellite glial cells and its receptor is up-regulated on both neurons and satellite cells in response to sciatic lesion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TGF-alpha and TGF-alpha receptor are differentially expressed in DRGs following a sciatic transection and that the differential expression may have different functional implications.
TGF-alpha and TGF-alpha receptor expression is upregulated in DRGs in response to peripheral nerve lesion.

TGF-alpha and the EGFR may play an important role in the plasticity of neurons and satellite cells following nerve injury, and that the expression pattern of these proteins is different in the ipsilateral vs contralateral DRG following nerve transection.
